teaser.text: China Shenhua Energy Company Limited is an integrated energy business built around coal. It earns money by extracting, moving and transforming that coal, while also selling the electricity and chemicals made from it.

stock.title: Shenhua stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Shenhua's forecast is broadly flat first, then modest by October 2029, with coal prices, cash after investment and dilution as the hinge.
stock.opening: Shenhua's weighted case is HKD41.71 in October 2027, with a roughly flat return. It hinges on Shenhua sustaining cash distributions per share after financing its mines, railways, ports and power assets.
stock.closing: The full memo answers how Shenhua makes money, compares with rivals, assesses management and examines its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Shenhua's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted price is HKD41.71 in October 2027, with dividends producing a roughly flat return from today’s HKD43.88. It reaches HKD40.83 in October 2028, for a 3% total return, and HKD40.12 in October 2029, for 6%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Shenhua, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case assumes weaker coal prices and demand, lower contract realizations, financing pressure and disappointing returns from acquired assets. It leads to HKD44.04 in 2027 and HKD42.25 in 2029. Its 30% probability reflects the fall in EBITDA from its 2022 peak, weaker coal sales and prices, higher unit costs and heavy capital spending.

The bull case requires resilient coal pricing, efficient integration and projects that ramp quickly enough to fund investment and dividends. It leads to HKD40.32 in 2027 and HKD38.22 in 2029. Its 20% probability reflects the absence of evidence that the acquired assets will immediately earn adequate returns.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Shenhua really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending rose from RMB36,814 million to RMB46,674 million. Free cash flow fell from RMB51,333 million to RMB25,539 million. Free cash flow is what remains after operating cash pays for long-lived assets, so it is closer than profit to the cash available for reinvestment or distribution.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Shenhua today?

paragraphs.text: China Shenhua Energy Company Limited’s H-share price already assumes durable earnings and generous distributions. At HK$43.88, investors must decide whether those earnings can survive a coal cycle and the enlarged group’s investment needs.

dividend.opening: Shenhua paid RMB3.24 per share in 2025, while its own free cash flow per share was RMB1.29. The dividend therefore exceeded the cash Shenhua generated per share that year.

blocks.heading: How much does Shenhua pay its shareholders per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from CNY1.90 per share in 2027 to CNY1.95 in 2028 and CNY2.00 in 2029. The bear case falls from CNY1.55 to CNY1.10, while the bull case rises from CNY2.15 to CNY2.55. The CNY0.98 interim dividend and CNY1.03 final dividend anchor the near-term base. But dividends already declined from CNY2.55 in 2022 to CNY2.01 in 2025, while 2025 dividends exceeded free cash flow.

blocks.heading: Does Shenhua’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: At HK$43.88, the H share trades at 13.2x trailing earnings; the 3.1% free-cash-flow yield is below the 5.4% dividend yield. Output was 332.1 million tonnes in 2025, while realised price fell to RMB495 per tonne from RMB563 in 2024. The company’s own free cash flow per share fell from RMB4.01 in 2022 to RMB1.29 in 2025. Dividends paid were RMB3.24 per share in 2025, RMB2.99 more than free cash flow.

Shenhua returned much of its operating cash while continuing to invest. Across the period, shareholder dividends and payments to minority owners of subsidiaries together exceeded free cash flow, and the gap became especially pronounced in the final year. The company could fund that difference from cash reserves, investment maturities or borrowing, but doing so reduced its financial cushion.

paragraphs.text: The outcome turns on coal prices and sales mix as contracts reset, and on whether acquired businesses improve chain economics. Hongshaquan No. 2 should enter formal production by the end of 2026; Boligou is expected in 2028. Xinjie’s initial working faces—the active underground areas where miners cut and remove coal—are targeted for 2029. Operating cash must cover the remaining 2026 capital plan and distributions while debt is refinanced. Contract coverage protects volume, not price, and 2025 dividends exceeded the company’s own free cash flow.

blocks.heading: What is Shenhua’s dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: Book value is HK$24.82 per share, so the 1.8x price-to-book ratio says investors pay for earning power beyond the accounting assets. The 3.1% free-cash-flow yield sits below the 5.4% dividend yield, making the cash reconciliation central. Shenhua also issued 1,363 million A shares and paid RMB85,791 million for acquired assets. New shares are more slices of the same cake: total profit can rise while each existing share gains less.

earnings.title: Shenhua earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Shenhua expects its next results on October 23, 2026, with guidance focused on coal production, sales, revenue, costs and capital spending.
earnings.opening: Shenhua expects its next results on October 23, 2026. Watch whether own-mine production catches up with the annual plan.
earnings.closing: The full Shenhua memo also answers Shenhua’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Shenhua plans to produce 513.4 million tonnes of commercial coal and sell 618.1 million tonnes. Commercial coal is coal prepared for sale, while sales also include coal bought from other producers. In the first quarter, Shenhua sold 78.0 million tonnes from its own mines and 25.2 million tonnes of purchased coal. That extra trading volume can increase revenue, but it usually contributes less profit than an additional tonne from Shenhua’s own mines.

Management also guides to a 4% rise in the unit production cost of self-produced coal. A unit cost is the cost of producing one tonne, not the company’s total spending. In the first quarter, revenue was RMB70.397 billion against RMB49.741 billion of cost of sales. Profit attributable to shareholders was RMB11.885 billion after further expenses and tax, so revenue less cost of sales is not the same as final profit.

blocks.heading: Has Shenhua kept its dividend promise?

paragraphs.text: The clearest measurable promise is the shareholder-return plan, approved in June 2025. It set a minimum annual cash distribution of 65% of attributable profit for 2025–2027, subject to the articles. Shenhua paid 79.1% of 2025 attributable profit as cash dividends, so it exceeded that floor.

blocks.heading: What is Shenhua’s revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: Subtracting March cumulative figures from June cumulative figures gives second-quarter revenue of RMB118,941 million. Derived operating income was RMB30,176 million, producing apparent revenue growth of 73.6% against June 2025. Derived attributable income was RMB19,169 million, with apparent growth of 43.8%.

The company’s comparable half-year figures are stronger evidence. Revenue rose 7.9%, attributable profit rose 1.9%, and EPS rose 0.7%. The quarterly table shows the reported sequence and its cumulative sources.
